recentItems.title: Alberta's Bill 25 sparks confusion in the classroom
recentItems.description:
Parts of An Act to Remove Politics and Ideology from Classrooms and Amend the Education Act are now in force in Alberta. One provision in the act says teachers must refrain from taking political or ideological stances in the classroom.

The province says the legislation is aimed at reinforcing neutrality in classrooms. But some teachers say they haven't received guidance around what constitutes a political or ideological stance and they're worried about falling afoul of rules they don't understand. And, they say, it compounds existing stressors like class sizes and complexities.

recentItems.title: Crisis in Sudan struggles to capture attention at UNGA
recentItems.description:
With world leaders at the UN general assembly grappling with mounting concern about AI development and an increasingly polarized geopolitical landscape, major humanitarian crises like the civil war in Sudan are struggling for attention. 

UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher discusses the human cost as leaders turn their attention away from humanitarianism and how organizations like the World Food Programme are struggling to keep up.

recentItems.title: Why Trump’s potash threat against Canada isn’t as bizarre as it sounds | About That
recentItems.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump is trying to lessen Canada's chokehold on potash supply with alternative imports from Belarus — but that's exposing a critical vulnerability in American agriculture. Andrew Chang breaks down why U.S. farmers depend so heavily on Saskatchewan’s vast potash reserves, and why relying on a Russian ally may be easier said than done.
